dailyTopNewsBrief.headline: Dolphins Drop to 1-9 After 26-9 Divisional Loss to Buffalo Bills
dailyTopNewsBrief.summary: Head coach Jeff Hafley's squad fell to 1-9 following a 26-9 home defeat to Buffalo, leaving Miami ranked last in scoring offense at 15.7 points per game. The Dolphins now prepare to host the 3-8 New York Jets in Week 12 holding a 0.1% playoff probability.
bullets: Miami struggled offensively in Sunday's 26-9 loss to Buffalo, failing to score a touchdown despite highlights like quarterback Kyle McCord's 21-yard pass to Malik Washington and Ollie Gordon II's 24-yard burst, as reported by [ESPN NFL Nation](https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401873070) and [miamidolphins.com Video](https://www.miamidolphins.com/video/mccord-locates-malik-washington-for-21-yard-connection).

On defense, linebackers Jordyn Brooks registered a nine-yard sack and Jacob Rodriguez intercepted a deflected Josh Allen pass, per [miamidolphins.com Video](https://www.miamidolphins.com/video/jordyn-brooks-enters-backfield-in-a-flash-for-9-yard-sack-on-josh-allen) and [miamidolphins.com Video](https://www.miamidolphins.com/video/jacob-rodriguez-eyes-down-josh-allen-s-deflected-pass-for-int).

Head coach Jeff Hafley addressed postgame execution concerns as Miami ranks 32nd in sacks per game (1.44) and net punt average (39.9 yards), detailed via [miamidolphins.com Video](https://www.miamidolphins.com/video/hc-jeff-hafley-nov-22-postgame-press-conference).

Looking ahead to Week 12, defensive coordinator Sean Duggan's unit carries the league's No. 2 Rush EPA allowed (-2.42) against New York, while Buffalo celebrated Sunday's win with social media jabs noted by [Anthony Gharib](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50567903/nfl-week-11-trolls).
